open_points.subject: A17 configuration path resolution
open_points.text: “a relative one from the working directory”
open_points.question: For later configuration re-reads, is a relative configuration path resolved from the startup working directory, from the process's then-current working directory, or converted to a stable directory-file-descriptor-relative path at startup?
options: Resolve afresh from the current working directory on every read
Anchor it to the startup working directory
Refuse relative configuration paths
open_points.default_guess: Anchor it to the startup working directory and reuse that stable anchor.

open_points.subject: A17 component file descriptors
open_points.text: “each directory on the way opened with `O_PATH` and `O_DIRECTORY`”
open_points.question: When are the directory and final-file descriptors closed, and must every such descriptor be close-on-exec so none can reach the sandbox or another child process?
options: Close all component descriptors immediately after the read and set close-on-exec
Keep directory descriptors for later re-reads but set close-on-exec
Leave descriptor lifetime and inheritance to the implementation
open_points.default_guess: Set close-on-exec on every descriptor and close all component descriptors after each checked read.

open_points.subject: A17 final path component
open_points.question: Which flags are used for the final component, particularly whether `O_CLOEXEC` and `O_NONBLOCK` are required so a FIFO or other non-regular object cannot block the kernel before the regular-file check?
options: Open with `O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC|O_NONBLOCK`, then verify it is regular
Open with `O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC`, accepting that a non-regular object may block
Open first with `O_PATH`, verify, then obtain a readable descriptor by a separately specified race-free method
open_points.default_guess: Use `O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC|O_NONBLOCK`, then verify the opened object is a regular file before reading.

open_points.subject: A18 data directory path
open_points.text: “At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory” and “Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links”
open_points.question: How is the data-directory path itself and each directory component resolved, and are symbolic links in that path refused or followed before the rule against links inside the directory begins?
options: Walk every component without following symbolic links
Allow links in the configured data-directory path but refuse links below the resolved directory
Resolve the path once by ordinary host path rules
open_points.default_guess: Walk the data-directory path component by component without following symbolic links and anchor all later access to the opened directory.

open_points.subject: A18 data directory bootstrap
open_points.text: “The data directory holds one SQLite database with every kernel record, a content-addressed area of value bytes and file fixtures named by digest, and the run spool”
open_points.question: What happens when the data directory, database, or required subdirectories are absent, have an unexpected type, or the database is unreadable or corrupt: which are created, which refuse startup, and in what order are these checks performed?
options: Create a missing directory and complete empty layout; refuse malformed or corrupt existing storage
Require the installer to create the directory but initialize an empty layout inside it
Require the complete layout and database to exist before startup
open_points.default_guess: Require an existing private data directory, create a missing empty internal layout atomically, and refuse unexpected types or a corrupt existing database.

open_points.subject: A18 private storage
open_points.text: “The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.”
open_points.question: What exact ownership and access test defines “private” for the directory, nested directories, database and sidecar files, stored values, fixtures, spool files and lock file, including ACLs?
options: Require ownership by the effective kernel UID and no group/other permission bits
Also reject ACLs granting access to another principal
Use only mode bits without checking ownership
open_points.default_guess: Require every object to be owned by the effective kernel UID, reject all group/other permission bits, and reject ACLs that grant another principal access.

open_points.subject: A18 exclusive lock
open_points.text: “At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory; a second process on the same directory refuses to start.”
open_points.question: What object and locking primitive define the lock, how are aliased paths or bind mounts of the same directory recognized, and what happens to a stale lock artifact after a crash?
options: Lock a fixed inode inside the opened directory with a kernel-released advisory lock
Lock the SQLite database using SQLite's own locking
Use exclusive creation of a lock file and define stale-lock recovery
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed lock file opened relative to the anchored directory and hold a kernel-released advisory lock for the process lifetime.

open_points.subject: A18 symlink checks
open_points.text: “Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links; a link found at start stops the start”
open_points.question: Does startup recursively inspect every object in every storage subtree, including directories, the database, SQLite journal/WAL files, lock files, temporary files and orphan files, and which failure is reported first when several links or other startup faults exist?
options: Recursively inspect all storage objects in a fixed path order before cleanup or database opening
Inspect only paths the startup procedure needs to open
Inspect each standard storage area separately with area-specific order
open_points.default_guess: Recursively inspect the entire storage tree in bytewise path order immediately after locking and refuse on the first symbolic link before cleanup or database access.

open_points.subject: A18 SQLite file opening
open_points.text: “Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links”
open_points.question: How is the no-symbolic-link rule enforced for the SQLite database and SQLite-created journal, WAL and shared-memory files without a check-then-open race inside the SQLite library?
options: Use a SQLite VFS that performs directory-relative no-follow opens
Pre-check paths and rely on the trusted host not to replace them
Exclude SQLite-managed sidecar files from the no-follow promise
open_points.default_guess: Use a directory-anchored SQLite VFS whose opens refuse symbolic links, including sidecar files.

open_points.subject: A18 store record order
open_points.text: “Activation M09 and FlowActivation M18 records are identified by their position in the store's one order of records” and “the store has one writer (K-17), so records have one order”
open_points.question: What exactly is a record's store position, and how are positions assigned among several records written by one transaction so activation identity, corpus order, recovery order and pagination are identical in every implementation?
options: One global monotonically increasing integer assigned in a specified insertion order
SQLite row order or row identifiers independently per table
A transaction position plus a per-transaction ordinal
open_points.default_guess: Use one global monotonically increasing position and assign it to records in the normative operation order before committing the transaction.

open_points.subject: A18 request serialization
open_points.text: “Surface requests are handled one at a time in the order they arrive”
open_points.question: At what event is a request considered to have arrived, and how are requests that are concurrently received or become complete together ordered?
options: Order by the single MCP transport parser's completed-message queue
Assign a global sequence when the first byte arrives
Allow any serialization order for simultaneous requests
open_points.default_guess: Assign a global sequence when a complete request is accepted from the MCP transport and process that queue in sequence order.

open_points.subject: A18 file and database atomicity
open_points.text: “Value bytes and spooled files are written to a temporary file, flushed, checked against their digest and size, and then renamed into place” and “A call that fails writes and changes no record; the only trace it can leave is a published file no record names”
open_points.question: What exact ordering and durability protocol relates temporary-file flush, rename, directory flush and SQLite commit so a committed record can never name a missing file after a crash?
options: Publish and durably flush every file and its directory before committing records
Commit records before publishing files and repair missing files on startup
Treat ordinary rename and SQLite commit as sufficient without directory durability
open_points.default_guess: Publish and fsync all files and containing directories before the SQLite commit; abort the transaction if publication fails.

open_points.subject: A18 filesystem requirements
open_points.question: Which filesystem guarantees are required for locking, atomic rename, durable flushes and SQLite transactions, and does startup refuse a filesystem on which A18's crash guarantees cannot be made?
options: Declare and check required filesystem semantics at startup
Support only a named set of local filesystems
Assume every Linux filesystem supplies the needed semantics without checking
open_points.default_guess: Declare the required semantics and refuse startup when the storage implementation can determine they are unavailable.

open_points.subject: A18 orphaned file fixtures
open_points.text: “On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... are removed”
open_points.question: Are file fixtures published by a failed capture call but named by no record also removed at startup, or are only unreferenced value bytes removed?
options: Remove every unreferenced content-addressed object, including fixtures
Remove only unreferenced value bytes and retain orphan fixtures
Use separate fixture cleanup rules
open_points.default_guess: Remove every unreferenced value-byte or fixture object at startup.

open_points.subject: A18 startup cleanup failures
open_points.text: “A spool directory that cannot be removed does not stop the start”
open_points.question: What happens when a temporary file or unreferenced value or fixture cannot be removed, since only failure to remove an obsolete spool directory is assigned behavior?
options: Refuse startup
Continue startup and leave every unremovable orphan unserved
Treat temporary files differently from unreferenced content objects
open_points.default_guess: Continue startup, leave the object unserved, and retry removal on the next startup.

open_points.subject: A18 existing digest target
open_points.text: “Equal bytes are stored once” and “a completed file a record names is never overwritten”
open_points.question: When publication finds an existing file at the digest-derived destination, how does the kernel establish that its bytes and size are equal, and what happens if they differ or the existing file is unreadable?
options: Read and verify the existing file; reuse only on equality and otherwise fail the store call
Trust the filename digest and reuse without reading
Replace an unreferenced destination but never a referenced one
open_points.default_guess: Verify the existing file's bytes, digest and size; reuse it only when equal and otherwise fail without writing records.

open_points.subject: A18 store compatibility across releases
open_points.text: “The data directory holds one SQLite database with every kernel record”
open_points.question: When a new release opens a database created by another release or schema version, does it migrate it, accept only compatible versions, or refuse startup?
options: Store a schema version and perform specified migrations
Accept only the exact schema version and refuse others
Attempt to open whatever schema is present
open_points.default_guess: Store an explicit schema version and refuse unsupported versions unless the release contains a defined transactional migration.

open_points.subject: A20 Linux support versus A18 guarantees
open_points.text: “A release runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named” and “Another system, or a Linux on which an open flag these rules name ... does not act as Linux documents it, is unsupported”
open_points.question: Is conforming behavior required on every Linux host with the named open-flag semantics even when its filesystem lacks the locking, rename, flush or SQLite guarantees A18 needs, or are those also host-support conditions?
options: Add A18's storage semantics to the unsupported-host conditions
Require conformance on every such Linux host and implement around filesystem differences
Restrict releases to named filesystem or mount configurations
open_points.default_guess: Treat the storage semantics required by A18 as additional support conditions.

open_points.subject: A20 sandbox startup probe
open_points.text: “the sandbox's facilities stay A03's, which the start probes” versus A03's “the start check ... asks only that a probe execution succeeds” and “the kernel does not inspect or verify at run time”
open_points.question: Does startup verify each required A03 isolation facility, or does it merely require one probe execution to succeed without establishing that namespaces, mounts and loopback behave as specified?
options: The probe explicitly verifies every A03 facility
The probe only has to execute successfully
The probe verifies a specified subset of A03 facilities
open_points.default_guess: Follow A03 literally: require bubblewrap to be present and one probe execution to succeed, without claiming that the probe independently verifies every facility.
